meaning: Enter or interrupt rudely, without waiting.
japanese: 断りもなく、割り込んで入ってくる。
cue: Someone walked into a closed meeting without knocking. Describe it.
reply: He barged in halfway through the review.
replyJapanese: 彼は評価の途中で、断りもなく入ってきました。
transferCue: Apologise for interrupting a conversation.
transferReply: Sorry to barge in — do you have two minutes afterwards?
transferReplyJapanese: 割り込んですみません。あとで2分いただけますか。
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces the person or conversation interrupted. Always sounds rude about someone else.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、割り込む相手や会話は on で示す。他人について使うとつねに無作法な響きになる。
contrast: Barge in enters rudely; butt in interrupts a conversation with words.
contrastJapanese: barge in は場に踏み込むこと。butt in は話に口を挟むこと。

meaning: Deliberately gain muscle or weight.
japanese: 体を大きくする。筋肉をつける。
cue: A friend has changed their training. Ask about it.
reply: Are you trying to bulk up, or just get stronger?
replyJapanese: 体を大きくしたいのですか、それとも力をつけたいだけですか。
transferCue: Describe an athlete's off-season.
transferReply: He bulked up over the winter and lost a little speed.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は冬のあいだに体を大きくして、少し速さを失いました。
nuance: Intransitive about people. Bulk something up instead means padding out a document.
nuanceJapanese: 人については自動詞。bulk something up なら、文書をかさ増しするという別の意味になる。
contrast: Bulk up adds mass on purpose; put on weight is neutral about intention.
contrastJapanese: bulk up は意図して体を大きくする。put on weight は意図を含まない。

meaning: Use up energy or remove something by burning.
japanese: 運動などで消費する。焼いて取り除く。
cue: A friend suggests a walk after a heavy lunch.
reply: Good idea — we can burn off some of that lunch.
replyJapanese: いいですね。昼食のぶんを少し消費できます。
transferCue: Describe morning fog on a hillside.
transferReply: The sun burns off the mist by about ten.
transferReplyJapanese: 10時ごろには、日差しが霧を消してしまいます。
nuance: Separable: burn it off. Used for calories, energy and for mist or fuel.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：burn it off。カロリーや体力のほか、霧や燃料にも使う。
contrast: Burn off consumes energy; burn out is exhausting yourself completely.
contrastJapanese: burn off はエネルギーを消費する。burn out は燃え尽きること。

meaning: Stop interfering in something that is not your business.
japanese: 口出しをやめる。
cue: You realise you have been advising on something private. Step back.
reply: I should butt out — it's your decision.
replyJapanese: 口出しはやめます。あなたが決めることです。
transferCue: Describe a family member who respects boundaries.
transferReply: She knows when to butt out, which is rare.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は引き際を心得ていて、そういう人はめったにいません。
nuance: Intransitive and informal. As a command it is rude, so it is safest about yourself.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけた表現。命令形は失礼なので、自分について使うのが無難。
contrast: Butt out withdraws from interfering; butt in starts interfering.
contrastJapanese: butt out は口出しをやめる。butt in は口を挟む。

meaning: Visit somewhere briefly on your way past.
japanese: 通りがかりに、ちょっと立ち寄る。
cue: You will be near a friend's office this afternoon.
reply: I'll call by around four if you're free.
replyJapanese: 時間が合えば、4時ごろ立ち寄ります。
transferCue: Describe an unexpected visitor.
transferReply: My neighbour called by with a parcel.
transferReplyJapanese: 隣の人が荷物を持って寄ってくれました。
nuance: Intransitive and British. It implies a short, informal visit while passing.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞でイギリス英語。通りがかりの、短く気軽な訪問を指す。
contrast: Call by is a brief visit in person; call back returns a phone call.
contrastJapanese: call by は短い訪問。call back は電話をかけ直すこと。

meaning: Do something difficult successfully.
japanese: 難しいことを、見事にやってのける。
cue: A colleague handled an awkward announcement well. Praise them.
reply: You carried it off better than I could have.
replyJapanese: 私にはできないほど、見事にやってのけましたね。
transferCue: Describe someone wearing an unusual outfit.
transferReply: Very few people could carry off that colour.
transferReplyJapanese: あの色を着こなせる人は、そう多くありません。
nuance: Separable: carry it off. It praises execution of something that could easily have failed.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：carry it off。失敗してもおかしくないことを、うまくやり切ったと評価する表現。
contrast: Carry off succeeds at something difficult; pull off stresses that it was unlikely.
contrastJapanese: carry off は難しいことをやり遂げる。pull off は成功が意外だったことを強調する。

meaning: Search in several directions for something.
japanese: あちこち探し回る。
cue: You need an idea and have no obvious source. Describe the search.
reply: I cast around for a venue and found nothing under budget.
replyJapanese: 会場をあちこち探しましたが、予算内のものはありませんでした。
transferCue: Describe looking for the right word mid-sentence.
transferReply: He cast around for a polite way to say no.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は、やんわり断る言い方を探していました。
nuance: Intransitive; for introduces what you seek. About and round are equally common.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、探す対象は for で示す。about や round も同じくらい使う。
contrast: Cast around searches broadly without a lead; track down pursues a specific target.
contrastJapanese: cast around は手がかりなく広く探す。track down は特定の対象を追う。

meaning: Switch from one system or method to another.
japanese: 別のやり方に切り替える。
cue: A team is moving to a new tool next month. Explain the plan.
reply: We change over to the new system on the first.
replyJapanese: 1日に新しいシステムへ切り替えます。
transferCue: Describe a household switching energy supplier.
transferReply: We changed over last spring and it was painless.
transferReplyJapanese: 昨春に切り替えましたが、手間はかかりませんでした。
nuance: Intransitive; to introduces the new system. The noun is a changeover, written as one word.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、切り替え先は to で示す。名詞は changeover と1語で書く。
contrast: Change over replaces one system with another; switch off simply stops something.
contrastJapanese: change over は体系ごと入れ替える。switch off は単に止めること。

meaning: Become too emotional to speak clearly.
japanese: 感極まって、声が詰まる。
cue: Describe someone giving a farewell speech.
reply: She choked up halfway through the thank-you.
replyJapanese: 感謝の言葉の途中で、彼女は声を詰まらせました。
transferCue: Describe your own reaction to a message.
transferReply: I choked up reading the card they signed.
transferReplyJapanese: みんなが署名したカードを読んで、思わず声が詰まりました。
nuance: Intransitive, often in the passive: get choked up. About emotion, not about physical choking.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、get choked up の形でもよく使う。物理的に詰まるのではなく、感情についての表現。
contrast: Choke up is being unable to speak; choke back is holding an emotion in.
contrastJapanese: choke up は声が出なくなること。choke back は感情を抑え込むこと。

meaning: Leave a place or experience with a particular impression.
japanese: ある印象を持って、その場をあとにする。
cue: You left a meeting feeling reassured. Describe it.
reply: I came away thinking they know what they're doing.
replyJapanese: 彼らは分かっていると感じながら、あの場をあとにしました。
transferCue: Describe what a visitor took from a museum.
transferReply: She came away with three pages of notes.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は3ページ分のメモを持って帰りました。
nuance: Intransitive; with introduces what you take, which can be an object or an impression.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、持ち帰るものは with で示す。物にも印象にも使える。
contrast: Come away leaves with something; get away is escaping a place.
contrastJapanese: come away は何かを得て立ち去る。get away はその場から逃れること。

meaning: Stop working suddenly, or fall asleep from exhaustion.
japanese: 突然動かなくなる。疲れて寝入る。
cue: Your car stopped on the way home. Tell a friend.
reply: The engine conked out just past the bridge.
replyJapanese: 橋を過ぎたあたりで、エンジンが止まってしまいました。
transferCue: Describe a child after a long day.
transferReply: He conked out before we reached the motorway.
transferReplyJapanese: 高速に入る前に、彼は寝入ってしまいました。
nuance: Intransitive and informal. Used for machines and, lightly, for people falling asleep.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけた表現。機械のほか、人が寝入る場合にも軽い調子で使う。
contrast: Conk out is a sudden stop; wear out is gradual exhaustion.
contrastJapanese: conk out は突然止まること。wear out は徐々にすり減ること。

meaning: Study intensively just before an exam.
japanese: 試験直前に、詰め込んで勉強する。
cue: A friend has an exam tomorrow. Ask about their evening.
reply: Are you cramming for it tonight, or have you given up?
replyJapanese: 今夜は詰め込みますか、それとももうあきらめましたか。
transferCue: Describe your own study habit.
transferReply: I always crammed for exams and forgot everything after.
transferReplyJapanese: いつも直前に詰め込んで、終わったら全部忘れていました。
nuance: Intransitive; for introduces the exam. It implies last-minute effort rather than steady study.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、試験は for で示す。着実な学習ではなく、土壇場の努力を含意する。
contrast: Cram for is last-minute study; brush up on refreshes what you already knew.
contrastJapanese: cram for は直前の詰め込み。brush up on は既に知っていることの復習。

meaning: Shout suddenly from pain, fear or surprise.
japanese: 痛みや驚きで、思わず声を上げる。
cue: Describe someone stepping on something sharp.
reply: She cried out and sat down on the step.
replyJapanese: 彼女は思わず声を上げて、段差に座り込みました。
transferCue: Describe a reaction at a surprise party.
transferReply: He cried out when the lights came on.
transferReplyJapanese: 明かりがついた瞬間、彼は声を上げました。
nuance: Intransitive. Be crying out for something is a separate sense: badly needing it.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。be crying out for something は「切実に必要としている」という別の意味。
contrast: Cry out is a sudden shout; call out is speaking to get attention.
contrastJapanese: cry out は思わず出る叫び。call out は注意を引くための呼びかけ。

meaning: Divide something into shares.
japanese: 分け前に分ける。
cue: A group needs to split a shared cost. Suggest the method.
reply: Let's divvy up the bill by what each of us ordered.
replyJapanese: 注文した分に応じて、勘定を分けましょう。
transferCue: Describe sharing out tasks.
transferReply: We divvied up the jobs before anyone arrived.
transferReplyJapanese: 誰かが来る前に、仕事を分担しておきました。
nuance: Separable: divvy it up. Informal; divide up is the neutral version.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：divvy it up。くだけた表現で、中立的には divide up と言う。
contrast: Divvy up splits into shares; club together pools money instead.
contrastJapanese: divvy up は分け合うこと。club together は逆に出し合うこと。

meaning: Move to a position behind others.
japanese: 後ろの位置まで下がる。
cue: Describe a runner during a long race.
reply: She dropped back on the hill and recovered later.
replyJapanese: 彼女は坂で遅れましたが、あとで持ち直しました。
transferCue: Describe walking as a group on a narrow path.
transferReply: I dropped back to let the others pass.
transferReplyJapanese: ほかの人を通すため、後ろに下がりました。
nuance: Intransitive and about position, not about quality. It can be deliberate or not.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、質ではなく位置についての表現。意図的な場合もそうでない場合もある。
contrast: Drop back moves behind; fall behind means losing ground you needed to keep.
contrastJapanese: drop back は後ろに下がる。fall behind は遅れを取ること。

meaning: Become completely dry, or lose necessary moisture.
japanese: すっかり乾く。乾燥しすぎる。
cue: Boots got soaked on a walk. Give advice.
reply: Let them dry out slowly, away from the radiator.
replyJapanese: 暖房から離して、ゆっくり乾かしてください。
transferCue: Describe a garden in a hot summer.
transferReply: The soil dried out completely in August.
transferReplyJapanese: 8月には、土がすっかり乾ききってしまいました。
nuance: Usually intransitive; dry something out is also possible. Dry off instead means removing surface water.
nuanceJapanese: ふつう自動詞だが、dry something out とも言える。表面の水気を取る場合は dry off を使う。
contrast: Dry out loses moisture throughout; dry off removes water from the surface.
contrastJapanese: dry out は中まで乾く。dry off は表面の水気を取る。

meaning: Leave quietly, or avoid a duty.
japanese: そっと抜け出す。義務を逃れる。
cue: You need to leave an event early without a fuss.
reply: I might duck out after the first talk.
replyJapanese: 最初の講演が終わったら、そっと抜けるかもしれません。
transferCue: Describe someone avoiding their share of a task.
transferReply: He ducked out of the clear-up again.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はまた、片づけを逃れました。
nuance: Intransitive; of introduces what is avoided. Leaving quietly is neutral, avoiding a duty is critical.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、逃れる対象は of で示す。静かに抜けるのは中立だが、義務逃れなら批判的になる。
contrast: Duck out leaves or avoids quietly; back out withdraws from something agreed.
contrastJapanese: duck out はそっと抜ける。back out は合意から降りること。

meaning: Start using something again after a long time.
japanese: 久しぶりに引っ張り出して、また使う。
cue: You are returning to an old hobby. Describe it.
reply: I dusted off my guitar for the first time in years.
replyJapanese: 何年ぶりかに、ギターを引っ張り出しました。
transferCue: Describe reusing an old proposal.
transferReply: We dusted off the plan from 2023 and updated it.
transferReplyJapanese: 2023年の案を引っ張り出して、手直ししました。
nuance: Separable: dust it off. Figurative as well as literal — skills and plans can be dusted off.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：dust it off。文字どおりの意味のほか、技能や計画にも比喩的に使う。
contrast: Dust off revives something unused; brush up on improves a skill you still use.
contrastJapanese: dust off は使っていなかったものを再び使う。brush up on は今も使う技能を磨き直す。

meaning: Become less intense, or try less hard.
japanese: 勢いがやわらぐ。手加減する。
cue: A colleague is working every evening. Suggest a change.
reply: Ease up a bit — the deadline moved to Friday.
replyJapanese: 少し力を抜いてください。締め切りは金曜に動きました。
transferCue: Describe the weather during a storm.
transferReply: The rain eased up around midnight.
transferReplyJapanese: 真夜中ごろ、雨が弱まりました。
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces what you do less of. Used for effort, pressure and weather.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、控える対象は on で示す。努力や圧力、天候について使う。
contrast: Ease up reduces intensity; give up stops altogether.
contrastJapanese: ease up は勢いを弱める。give up は完全にやめる。

meaning: Gradually destroy or reduce something.
japanese: 少しずつ蝕んで、減らしていく。
cue: Repeated small costs have reduced a budget. Describe it.
reply: The extra fees are eating away at the margin.
replyJapanese: 追加の手数料が、利益をじわじわ削っています。
transferCue: Describe a coastline over time.
transferReply: The sea has eaten away at the cliff for centuries.
transferReplyJapanese: 海は何世紀もかけて、崖を削ってきました。
nuance: Usually with at. It suits slow damage, including worry eating away at someone.
nuanceJapanese: ふつう at を伴う。ゆっくりした損耗に合い、心配事が人を蝕む場合にも使う。
contrast: Eat away erodes gradually; eat into takes a noticeable share of something.
contrastJapanese: eat away は徐々に侵食する。eat into はまとまった分を食い込んで奪う。

meaning: Become more equal or more level.
japanese: ばらつきが減って、平らになる。
cue: Workload was uneven and has settled. Report it.
reply: The hours evened out once we shared the rota.
replyJapanese: 当番を分け合ってから、時間のばらつきが減りました。
transferCue: Describe prices after a busy season.
transferReply: Fares even out again in October.
transferReplyJapanese: 運賃は10月にまた落ち着きます。
nuance: Intransitive, or even something out. About distribution over time or between people.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞だが even something out とも言える。時間や人のあいだの配分についての表現。
contrast: Even out balances a distribution; average out reports the resulting mean.
contrastJapanese: even out は配分を均す。average out はその結果の平均を述べる。

meaning: Gradually become weaker until it disappears.
japanese: だんだん弱まって、消えていく。
cue: An old rivalry stopped mattering. Describe it.
reply: The argument faded away once they started working together.
replyJapanese: 一緒に働き始めてから、あの対立は自然に消えました。
transferCue: Describe the end of a song.
transferReply: The last note fades away instead of stopping.
transferReplyJapanese: 最後の音は、止まるのではなく消えていきます。
nuance: Intransitive. It describes gradual disappearance, not a decision to stop.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。やめる決断ではなく、自然に消えていく様子を表す。
contrast: Fade away disappears gradually; die down is noise or excitement settling.
contrastJapanese: fade away は徐々に消える。die down は騒ぎや興奮が収まること。

meaning: Decrease sharply, or come loose and drop off.
japanese: 急に減る。外れて落ちる。
cue: Attendance dropped after a change. Report it.
reply: Numbers fell away after the fee was introduced.
replyJapanese: 料金の導入後、人数が急に減りました。
transferCue: Describe old plaster on a wall.
transferReply: The paint is falling away in the corner.
transferReplyJapanese: 隅のほうで、塗装が剥がれ落ちています。
nuance: Intransitive. Sharper than fade away, and it can describe support or numbers as well as material.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。fade away より急激で、物のほか支持や人数にも使う。
contrast: Fall away is a sharp decline; tail off is a gentle one.
contrastJapanese: fall away は急な落ち込み。tail off は緩やかな減少。

meaning: Move back, or reduce in number or level.
japanese: 後退する。数値が下がる。
cue: A figure rose then returned to normal. Describe it.
reply: Sales spiked in July and fell back in August.
replyJapanese: 売上は7月に跳ね上がり、8月に戻りました。
transferCue: Describe a crowd giving way.
transferReply: The crowd fell back to let the ambulance through.
transferReplyJapanese: 救急車を通すため、人だかりが後ろに下がりました。
nuance: Intransitive. Fall back on something is a separate sense: use it when nothing else works.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。fall back on something は「頼みの綱にする」という別の意味。
contrast: Fall back returns to a lower level; fall behind means failing to keep pace.
contrastJapanese: fall back は水準が戻ること。fall behind は遅れを取ること。

meaning: Spread out from one point across an area.
japanese: 一点から広がって、散らばる。
cue: A search party is organising itself. Give the instruction.
reply: Let's fan out from the car park and meet at the gate.
replyJapanese: 駐車場から散らばって、門で落ち合いましょう。
transferCue: Describe a river reaching the sea.
transferReply: The channels fan out across the delta.
transferReplyJapanese: 水路は三角州一帯に広がっています。
nuance: Intransitive; from introduces the starting point. It implies a widening shape.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、起点は from で示す。扇状に広がる形を含意する。
contrast: Fan out spreads from a point; spread out is neutral about the shape.
contrastJapanese: fan out は一点から扇状に広がる。spread out は形を問わない。

meaning: Touch or adjust something repeatedly, often absent-mindedly.
japanese: 無意識に、しきりにいじる。
cue: Someone kept touching their pen during an interview. Describe it.
reply: He fiddled with his pen the whole time.
replyJapanese: 彼はずっとペンをいじっていました。
transferCue: Describe adjusting a setting you do not understand.
transferReply: Don't fiddle with the thermostat — I've just set it.
transferReplyJapanese: 温度調節はいじらないで。設定したばかりです。
nuance: Inseparable. It suggests small pointless adjustments, so it is mildly negative.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。意味のない細かい操作を指すので、やや否定的。
contrast: Fiddle with is aimless handling; tinker with is adjusting to improve something.
contrastJapanese: fiddle with は目的のないいじり方。tinker with は改善のための調整。

meaning: Resist an attack or a difficulty.
japanese: 反撃する。負けずに立ち向かう。
cue: A team was losing badly and recovered. Describe it.
reply: They fought back in the second half and drew.
replyJapanese: 後半に巻き返して、彼らは引き分けました。
transferCue: Describe holding in tears.
transferReply: She fought back tears during the speech.
transferReplyJapanese: 挨拶のあいだ、彼女は涙をこらえていました。
nuance: Intransitive with against, or transitive with tears. Fight is irregular: fought.
nuanceJapanese: against を伴う自動詞用法と、tears を目的語に取る用法がある。fight は不規則変化で fought。
contrast: Fight back resists; fight off drives an attack or illness away.
contrastJapanese: fight back は抵抗する。fight off は攻撃や病気を撃退する。

meaning: Succeed in resisting an attack, an illness or a feeling.
japanese: 病気や攻撃、眠気などを撃退する。
cue: A colleague looks unwell but is still working. Comment.
reply: I've been fighting off a cold all week.
replyJapanese: 今週はずっと、風邪を寄せつけないようにしています。
transferCue: Describe staying awake in a long meeting.
transferReply: I fought off sleep for the last twenty minutes.
transferReplyJapanese: 最後の20分は、眠気と戦っていました。
nuance: Separable: fight it off. Used for illness, sleep, rivals and attackers.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：fight it off。病気や眠気、競合相手、襲撃者に使う。
contrast: Fight off repels something; shake off is getting free of it afterwards.
contrastJapanese: fight off は寄せつけない。shake off はあとから振り払うこと。

meaning: Make someone enthusiastic, or start a machine.
japanese: やる気を起こさせる。機械を起動する。
cue: A talk energised the team. Describe the effect.
reply: That talk really fired everyone up.
replyJapanese: あの話で、みんなすっかりやる気になりました。
transferCue: Describe starting equipment in the morning.
transferReply: Fire up the machine and I'll bring the coffee.
transferReplyJapanese: 機械を立ち上げてください。コーヒーは私が持ってきます。
nuance: Separable: fire them up. People get fired up; machines get fired up too.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：fire them up。人にも機械にも使える。
contrast: Fire up creates enthusiasm; wind up can mean deliberately annoying someone.
contrastJapanese: fire up は熱意をかき立てる。wind up はわざといらだたせる意味にもなる。

meaning: Make something more definite.
japanese: 内容をはっきり固める。
cue: A rough plan needs detail before it is shared.
reply: Let's firm up the dates before we tell anyone.
replyJapanese: 誰かに伝える前に、日程を固めましょう。
transferCue: Describe a provisional booking.
transferReply: The hotel is held but not firmed up yet.
transferReplyJapanese: ホテルは押さえていますが、まだ確定ではありません。
nuance: Separable: firm it up. About plans and arrangements rather than physical hardness.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：firm it up。物の硬さではなく、計画や手配について使う。
contrast: Firm up makes a plan definite; nail down settles a detail that was disputed.
contrastJapanese: firm up は計画を確定させる。nail down は揉めていた細部を決着させる。

meaning: Signal to a vehicle to make it stop.
japanese: 合図して、車を止める。
cue: You need a taxi in the street.
reply: Let's flag down a taxi on the main road.
replyJapanese: 大通りでタクシーを拾いましょう。
transferCue: Describe getting help on a quiet road.
transferReply: We flagged down a passing van.
transferReplyJapanese: 通りかかったバンを止めて、助けを求めました。
nuance: Separable: flag it down. Only for vehicles, and it implies a visible arm signal.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：flag it down。乗り物にのみ使い、手を振る合図を含意する。
contrast: Flag down stops a vehicle; pull over is the driver stopping at the side.
contrastJapanese: flag down は外から車を止めさせる。pull over は運転手が脇に寄せること。

meaning: Draw attention to something so people notice it.
japanese: 気づいてもらえるよう、指摘しておく。
cue: You spotted a risk that others may miss. Raise it.
reply: I wanted to flag up the licence renewal before March.
replyJapanese: 3月の前に、ライセンス更新の件を指摘しておきたいです。
transferCue: Describe what a reviewer did with a draft.
transferReply: She flagged up two sections that needed sources.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は、出典が必要な2か所を指摘してくれました。
nuance: Separable: flag it up. British and common at work; American English says flag or raise.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：flag it up。イギリス英語で職場でよく使う。アメリカ英語では flag や raise と言う。
contrast: Flag up raises something for attention; point out corrects a specific fact.
contrastJapanese: flag up は注意を促す。point out は具体的な事実を指摘する。

meaning: Stop rising or falling and become level.
japanese: 上下の動きが止まり、横ばいになる。
cue: A growth curve has stopped climbing. Describe it.
reply: Growth flattened out after the second quarter.
replyJapanese: 第2四半期以降、成長は横ばいになりました。
transferCue: Describe a mountain road.
transferReply: The path flattens out after the treeline.
transferReplyJapanese: 森林限界を過ぎると、道は平坦になります。
nuance: Intransitive. Used for graphs, roads and trends alike.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。グラフや道路、傾向のいずれにも使う。
contrast: Flatten out becomes level; level off is an equally common alternative.
contrastJapanese: flatten out は横ばいになる。level off もほぼ同じ意味で使える。

meaning: Get rid of someone with an excuse instead of helping.
japanese: 言い訳でごまかして、あしらう。
cue: A customer got three different excuses. Describe it.
reply: They fobbed her off with a promise to call back.
replyJapanese: 折り返すと言われただけで、彼女はあしらわれました。
transferCue: Insist on a real answer.
transferReply: I don't want to be fobbed off again.
transferReplyJapanese: また言い訳でごまかされたくありません。
nuance: Separable: fob them off. With introduces the excuse. Always critical.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：fob them off。言い訳は with で示す。つねに批判的。
contrast: Fob off dismisses with an excuse; brush off dismisses without one.
contrastJapanese: fob off は言い訳であしらう。brush off は理由もなく突き放す。

meaning: Behave playfully instead of being serious.
japanese: まじめにやらず、ふざける。
cue: Two people are joking during a safety briefing. Ask them to stop.
reply: Let's not fool around until the briefing is over.
replyJapanese: 説明が終わるまでは、ふざけるのはやめましょう。
transferCue: Describe a relaxed afternoon.
transferReply: We fooled around with the camera for an hour.
transferReplyJapanese: 1時間ほど、カメラで遊んでいました。
nuance: Intransitive; with introduces what you play with. British English also says fool about.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、遊ぶ対象は with で示す。イギリス英語では fool about とも言う。
contrast: Fool around is playful time-wasting; mess up is actually spoiling something.
contrastJapanese: fool around はふざけて時間を使うこと。mess up は実際に台なしにすること。

meaning: Pay a lot of money, usually unwillingly.
japanese: しぶしぶ大金を払う。
cue: A repair cost far more than expected. React.
reply: We had to fork out three hundred for the boiler.
replyJapanese: ボイラーに300も払う羽目になりました。
transferCue: Describe the cost of a concert ticket.
transferReply: People forked out a fortune for those seats.
transferReplyJapanese: あの席には、みんな大枚をはたきました。
nuance: Informal; for introduces what you paid for. Always implies reluctance.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、支払い対象は for で示す。つねに気が進まない含みがある。
contrast: Fork out stresses the amount; cough up stresses the reluctance.
contrastJapanese: fork out は金額の大きさ、cough up は気の進まなさを強調する。

meaning: Spoil something by doing it badly.
japanese: へまをして、台なしにする。
cue: A booking error affected a whole trip. Own it.
reply: I fouled up the dates and we lost the deposit.
replyJapanese: 日付を間違えて、手付金を失いました。
transferCue: Describe a delivery problem.
transferReply: The courier fouled up the address again.
transferReplyJapanese: 配送業者がまた住所を間違えました。
nuance: Separable: foul it up. Informal; the noun is a foul-up, written with a hyphen.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：foul it up。くだけた表現で、名詞は foul-up とハイフンでつなぐ。
contrast: Foul up spoils through error; mess up is the more everyday word.
contrastJapanese: foul up はミスで台なしにする。mess up のほうが日常的な語。

meaning: Make something available that was being used.
japanese: ふさがっていたものを、使える状態にする。
cue: Cancelling a meeting creates time. Describe the gain.
reply: Dropping that call frees up an hour on Thursday.
replyJapanese: あの通話をやめれば、木曜に1時間空きます。
transferCue: Describe reorganising storage.
transferReply: Moving the boxes freed up the whole corner.
transferReplyJapanese: 箱を動かしたら、隅がまるごと空きました。
nuance: Separable: free it up. Used for time, space, money and people.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：free it up。時間や場所、資金、人手について使う。
contrast: Free up makes a resource available; clear out empties a space entirely.
contrastJapanese: free up は資源を使える状態にする。clear out は場所を空にする。

meaning: Deliberately exclude someone from a group.
japanese: 意図的に、仲間はずれにする。
cue: A colleague stopped being invited to things. Describe it.
reply: They froze him out after the disagreement.
replyJapanese: あの対立のあと、彼は仲間はずれにされました。
transferCue: Describe a company losing access to a market.
transferReply: Smaller firms were frozen out of the bidding.
transferReplyJapanese: 小規模の会社は、入札から締め出されました。
nuance: Separable: freeze them out. Freeze is irregular: froze, frozen. It implies deliberate exclusion.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：freeze them out。freeze は不規則変化で froze、frozen。意図的な排除を含意する。
contrast: Freeze out excludes socially; crowd out squeezes something aside by volume.
contrastJapanese: freeze out は人間関係で締め出す。crowd out は量で押しのける。

meaning: Join together against one person.
japanese: 徒党を組んで、一人を攻撃する。
cue: Several people criticised one colleague at once. Describe it.
reply: It felt like everyone ganged up on her.
replyJapanese: みんなで彼女を攻めているように感じました。
transferCue: Describe children playing unfairly.
transferReply: They ganged up on the youngest again.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らはまた、いちばん下の子を寄ってたかって攻めました。
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces the target. Always disapproving.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、対象は on で示す。つねに否定的。
contrast: Gang up is many against one; close ranks is a group defending itself.
contrastJapanese: gang up は大勢で一人を攻める。close ranks は集団が身を守ること。

meaning: Worry someone persistently.
japanese: 気がかりが、じわじわ心を苛む。
cue: A small doubt has stayed with you all week. Describe it.
reply: The question has been gnawing at me since Monday.
replyJapanese: 月曜からずっと、その疑問が頭を離れません。
transferCue: Describe lingering guilt.
transferReply: It gnawed at him until he finally apologised.
transferReplyJapanese: 謝るまで、そのことが彼を苛み続けました。
nuance: Inseparable; the worry is the subject. Usually in the continuous form.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、主語は気がかりのほう。ふつうは進行形で使う。
contrast: Gnaw at is persistent worry; dwell on is choosing to keep thinking about something.
contrastJapanese: gnaw at は勝手に苛むもの。dwell on は自ら考え続けること。

meaning: Wear away someone's resistance or spirit over time.
japanese: 時間をかけて、気力をすり減らす。
cue: A long dispute has exhausted someone. Describe it.
reply: Two years of appeals will grind anyone down.
replyJapanese: 2年も不服申し立てが続けば、誰でもすり減ります。
transferCue: Describe a demanding commute.
transferReply: The daily travel grinds you down eventually.
transferReplyJapanese: 毎日の移動は、いずれ気力を削っていきます。
nuance: Separable: grind them down. The cause is the subject. Grind is irregular (ground), which reads the same as the noun, so the base form is clearer.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：grind them down。主語は原因のほう。grind の過去形 ground は名詞と同形なので、原形のほうが誤解がない。
contrast: Grind down exhausts resistance; wear out exhausts energy.
contrastJapanese: grind down は抵抗する気力を削る。wear out は体力を消耗させる。

meaning: Try hard to get something, or try to harm someone.
japanese: ねらって全力で動く。人を攻撃しようとする。
cue: A colleague is openly pursuing a promotion. Describe it.
reply: She's gunning for the lead role this year.
replyJapanese: 彼女は今年、主任の座をねらっています。
transferCue: Describe a rival team's intent.
transferReply: They'll be gunning for us after last season.
transferReplyJapanese: 昨季のこともあって、彼らは本気で来るでしょう。
nuance: Inseparable and informal, usually in the continuous. For a goal it is neutral; for a person it is hostile.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できないくだけた表現で、ふつう進行形。目標には中立、人に向けると敵対的。
contrast: Gun for pursues aggressively; go for is a plain choice or attempt.
contrastJapanese: gun for は激しく追い求める。go for は単に選ぶ・試みること。

meaning: Pass something to each person in a group.
japanese: その場の全員に、順に配る。
cue: You have brought food to share at a meeting.
reply: Could you hand round the biscuits while I pour?
replyJapanese: 注ぎますので、ビスケットを回していただけますか。
transferCue: Describe distributing documents.
transferReply: She handed round the agenda before we started.
transferReplyJapanese: 始める前に、彼女が議事次第を配りました。
nuance: Separable: hand them round. British; American English says hand around.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：hand them round。イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では hand around と言う。
contrast: Hand round gives to everyone present; hand out can be to a wider group.
contrastJapanese: hand round はその場の全員に配る。hand out はより広い相手にも使える。

meaning: Remind you of something from the past.
japanese: 過去のことを思い起こさせる。
cue: A new design resembles an older era. Describe it.
reply: The lettering harks back to 1930s posters.
replyJapanese: あの書体は、1930年代のポスターを思わせます。
transferCue: Describe a colleague who often mentions the past.
transferReply: He harks back to how things were before the merger.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は合併前のやり方を、よく引き合いに出します。
nuance: Inseparable and slightly formal. About people it can be mildly critical of nostalgia.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない、やや改まった表現。人について使うと、懐古的だという軽い批判になる。
contrast: Hark back to evokes the past; look back on is deliberately reviewing it.
contrastJapanese: hark back to は過去を想起させる。look back on は意識的に振り返ること。

meaning: Surround someone so they cannot move freely.
japanese: 取り囲んで、動きを封じる。
cue: Rules leave a team almost no choices. Describe the feeling.
reply: The conditions hem us in on every side.
replyJapanese: あの条件に、四方から囲まれている状態です。
transferCue: Describe a narrow valley.
transferReply: The village is hemmed in by steep hills.
transferReplyJapanese: その村は、険しい丘に囲まれています。
nuance: Separable but very often passive: be hemmed in by. Used for geography and for constraints.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できるが、be hemmed in by の受け身で使うことが非常に多い。地形にも制約にも使う。
contrast: Hem in surrounds and confines; box in blocks the way out of a specific space.
contrastJapanese: hem in は周囲から閉じ込める。box in は特定の場所からの出口を塞ぐ。

meaning: Depend entirely on one thing.
japanese: ただ一点に、すべてがかかっている。
cue: One approval decides a whole project. Say so.
reply: The whole plan hinges on the permit.
replyJapanese: 計画全体が、あの許可にかかっています。
transferCue: Describe a decision that depends on one number.
transferReply: It hinges on whether the rent goes up.
transferReplyJapanese: 家賃が上がるかどうかに、すべてがかかっています。
nuance: Inseparable. Stronger than depend on: it names a single decisive factor.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。depend on より強く、決定的な一点を指す。
contrast: Hinge on names one decisive factor; depend on allows several.
contrastJapanese: hinge on は決定的な一点。depend on は複数の要因を許す。

meaning: Separate part of an organisation and make it independent.
japanese: 一部門を切り離して、独立させる。
cue: A division became its own company. Report it.
reply: They hived off the research arm last year.
replyJapanese: 昨年、研究部門が切り離されました。
transferCue: Describe a proposal for a service.
transferReply: The plan is to hive off maintenance into a separate team.
transferReplyJapanese: 保守を切り離して、別チームにする案です。
nuance: Separable: hive it off. British and mostly used about businesses and departments.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：hive it off。イギリス英語で、企業や部門について使うのがほとんど。
contrast: Hive off separates a unit; spin off usually creates a new company from it.
contrastJapanese: hive off は部門を切り離す。spin off はそこから新会社を作ることが多い。

meaning: Refuse to accept less than what you want.
japanese: 望む条件が出るまで、引き下がらない。
cue: An offer is below your minimum. State your position.
reply: I'd hold out for the full amount.
replyJapanese: 満額が出るまで、引き下がらないほうがいいでしょう。
transferCue: Describe waiting for the right flat.
transferReply: They held out for a garden and waited eight months.
transferReplyJapanese: 庭付きにこだわって、彼らは8か月待ちました。
nuance: Inseparable; for introduces what you insist on. It implies patience as well as refusal.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、こだわる条件は for で示す。拒否だけでなく、待つ忍耐も含意する。
contrast: Hold out for waits for better terms; stand your ground refuses to move at all.
contrastJapanese: hold out for はよい条件を待つ。stand your ground は一歩も引かないこと。

meaning: Force someone to leave through constant pressure.
japanese: 執拗な圧力で、辞めさせる。
cue: A public figure resigned after sustained criticism. Describe it.
reply: He was hounded out of the job within a month.
replyJapanese: 1か月のうちに、彼は執拗な攻撃で職を追われました。
transferCue: Describe why someone left a club.
transferReply: She felt hounded out rather than asked to go.
transferReplyJapanese: 辞めるよう言われたというより、追い出されたと彼女は感じています。
nuance: Separable and usually passive: be hounded out. Of introduces the job or place.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できるが、be hounded out の受け身がふつう。職や場所は of で示す。
contrast: Hound out forces someone out by pressure; freeze out excludes them quietly.
contrastJapanese: hound out は圧力で追い出す。freeze out は静かに締め出す。

meaning: Settle in and prepare to wait out something difficult.
japanese: 腰を据えて、じっと持ちこたえる。
cue: A difficult quarter is ahead. Describe the approach.
reply: We'll hunker down and get through the winter.
replyJapanese: 腰を据えて、冬を乗り切りましょう。
transferCue: Describe a household before a storm.
transferReply: We hunkered down with candles and waited.
transferReplyJapanese: ろうそくを用意して、じっと待ちました。
nuance: Intransitive and informal. It implies staying put rather than acting.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけた表現。動くのではなく、その場に留まることを含意する。
contrast: Hunker down waits something out; ride out survives it without the sense of hiding.
contrastJapanese: hunker down は身を潜めて待つ。ride out は身を潜める含みなく乗り切ること。

meaning: Search until you find someone or something.
japanese: 見つかるまで、徹底的に探す。
cue: A missing document turned up after a long search.
reply: I hunted down the original contract in the archive.
replyJapanese: 書庫で、元の契約書を探し出しました。
transferCue: Describe finding a rare item.
transferReply: She hunted down a replacement part online.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はネットで、交換部品を探し出しました。
nuance: Separable: hunt it down. It implies persistence, not a quick look.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：hunt it down。ざっと探すのではなく、粘り強さを含意する。
contrast: Hunt down finds after searching; track down is a close alternative.
contrastJapanese: hunt down は探し当てる。track down もほぼ同じ意味。

meaning: Stop information from becoming public.
japanese: 表沙汰にならないよう、もみ消す。
cue: An incident was never reported. Describe the claim.
reply: The report says the whole thing was hushed up.
replyJapanese: 報告書は、その件がもみ消されたとしています。
transferCue: Argue for openness.
transferReply: Trying to hush it up would make it worse.
transferReplyJapanese: もみ消そうとすれば、かえって悪化します。
nuance: Separable: hush it up. Always disapproving, and often passive.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：hush it up。つねに否定的で、受け身で使うことも多い。
contrast: Hush up suppresses information; gloss over mentions it but minimises it.
contrastJapanese: hush up は情報を隠す。gloss over は触れつつ軽く扱う。

meaning: Make something more interesting or attractive.
japanese: 手を加えて、見栄えや面白みを足す。
cue: A plain room needs improving cheaply. Suggest something.
reply: We could jazz it up with a rug and a lamp.
replyJapanese: ラグとランプで、少し華やかにできますよ。
transferCue: Describe improving a simple dish.
transferReply: A bit of lemon jazzes up the whole thing.
transferReplyJapanese: レモンを少し加えるだけで、ぐっとよくなります。
nuance: Separable: jazz it up. Informal, and about surface appeal rather than substance.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：jazz it up。くだけた表現で、中身より見た目や印象についての語。
contrast: Jazz up adds appeal; spruce up makes something tidy and fresh.
contrastJapanese: jazz up は華やかさを足す。spruce up はきれいに整えること。

meaning: Become a member, or connect separate parts.
japanese: 入会する。ばらばらのものをつなぐ。
cue: A friend is considering a local club.
reply: You should join up — the first month is free.
replyJapanese: 入会するといいですよ。最初の1か月は無料です。
transferCue: Describe connecting two paths.
transferReply: The two routes join up beyond the bridge.
transferReplyJapanese: 2つの道は、橋の先で合流します。
nuance: Intransitive for membership; join something up connects parts. Joined-up thinking means well connected.
nuanceJapanese: 入会の意味では自動詞。join something up なら部分をつなぐ意味。joined-up thinking は筋の通った考えという意味。
contrast: Join up becomes a member; join in takes part in an activity already happening.
contrastJapanese: join up は会員になる。join in は進行中の活動に加わる。

meaning: Fall over suddenly.
japanese: ばったりと倒れる。
cue: Describe someone fainting in the heat.
reply: He nearly keeled over in the queue.
replyJapanese: 彼は列の中で、倒れそうになりました。
transferCue: Describe a tree after a storm.
transferReply: The old pine keeled over in the night.
transferReplyJapanese: 夜のうちに、あの古い松が倒れました。
nuance: Intransitive and informal. It suggests a sudden fall, often from illness or wind.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけた表現。病気や風などによる、突然の転倒を表す。
contrast: Keel over falls suddenly; pass out is losing consciousness.
contrastJapanese: keel over は突然倒れること。pass out は意識を失うこと。

meaning: Type information into a system.
japanese: データを入力する。
cue: Explain a step in a process.
reply: Key in the reference before you press submit.
replyJapanese: 送信を押す前に、参照番号を入力してください。
transferCue: Describe a data-entry job.
transferReply: She keyed in four hundred records in a day.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は1日で400件を入力しました。
nuance: Separable: key it in. Slightly dated; type in or enter is more common now.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：key it in。やや古い言い方で、今は type in や enter が一般的。
contrast: Key in types data; log in identifies you to a system.
contrastJapanese: key in はデータを打ち込む。log in はシステムに自分を認識させる。

meaning: Discuss an idea informally.
japanese: 案を気楽に出し合って検討する。
cue: A team needs early ideas, not decisions.
reply: Let's kick a few ideas around before Friday.
replyJapanese: 金曜までに、いくつか案を出し合ってみましょう。
transferCue: Describe an informal planning session.
transferReply: We kicked the proposal around over lunch.
transferReplyJapanese: 昼食のときに、その提案を気楽に検討しました。
nuance: Separable: kick it around. Informal, and it implies no commitment yet.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：kick it around。くだけた表現で、まだ決定ではないことを含意する。
contrast: Kick around explores ideas loosely; thrash out reaches an agreement.
contrastJapanese: kick around は気楽に案を出す。thrash out は結論まで詰める。

meaning: Stop work for the day, or reduce a price.
japanese: 仕事を切り上げる。値引きする。
cue: It is late and the work can wait. Suggest stopping.
reply: Shall we knock off and finish in the morning?
replyJapanese: 今日は切り上げて、朝に仕上げませんか。
transferCue: Describe a discount at a market.
transferReply: He knocked off ten pounds for cash.
transferReplyJapanese: 現金払いで、彼は10ポンド引いてくれました。
nuance: Intransitive for finishing work; separable for a price: knock it off. Knock it off! also means stop that.
nuanceJapanese: 仕事を終える意味では自動詞、値引きでは分離可能。knock it off! は「やめて」という別の意味。
contrast: Knock off ends the working day; clock off records that you have left.
contrastJapanese: knock off は仕事を切り上げる。clock off は退勤を記録すること。

meaning: Fasten shoes or boots with laces.
japanese: 靴ひもを結ぶ。
cue: You are getting ready for a walk.
reply: Give me a second to lace up my boots.
replyJapanese: ブーツのひもを結ぶので、少し待ってください。
transferCue: Describe a runner before a race.
transferReply: She laced up her shoes and went to the line.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は靴のひもを結んで、スタートラインに向かいました。
nuance: Separable: lace them up. The adjective is lace-up, as in lace-up boots.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：lace them up。形容詞は lace-up で、lace-up boots のように使う。
contrast: Lace up fastens laces; do up fastens any kind of clothing.
contrastJapanese: lace up はひもを結ぶ。do up は留め具全般に使える。

meaning: End up somewhere or in some state, unintentionally.
japanese: 思いがけず、ある場所や状態に行き着く。
cue: A journey went wrong. Describe where you ended.
reply: We landed up in a town nobody had heard of.
replyJapanese: 誰も知らない町に行き着いてしまいました。
transferCue: Describe an unplanned career.
transferReply: He landed up teaching, which he never planned.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は思いがけず、教える仕事に落ち着きました。
nuance: Intransitive and British; American English says end up. It implies the result was not planned.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞でイギリス英語。アメリカ英語では end up と言う。計画外の結果を含意する。
contrast: Land up is an unplanned outcome; settle down is choosing to stay somewhere.
contrastJapanese: land up は意図しない結果。settle down は自ら落ち着くこと。

meaning: Treat something as unimportant by joking about it.
japanese: 冗談にして、軽く受け流す。
cue: Someone made light of a minor injury. Describe it.
reply: She laughed it off and carried on playing.
replyJapanese: 彼女は笑って受け流し、そのまま続けました。
transferCue: Advise against dismissing a concern.
transferReply: I wouldn't laugh off a warning like that.
transferReplyJapanese: あの種の警告を、笑って流さないほうがいいでしょう。
nuance: Separable: laugh it off. It can show resilience or unwise dismissal, depending on what is dismissed.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：laugh it off。受け流す対象によって、強さにも軽率さにもなる。
contrast: Laugh off dismisses with humour; shrug off dismisses without reacting at all.
contrastJapanese: laugh off は笑って流す。shrug off は反応せずに流す。

meaning: Start doing or saying something with energy, often at length.
japanese: 勢いよく、長々と始める。
cue: A colleague started a long explanation unprompted. Describe it.
reply: He launched into the history of the project.
replyJapanese: 彼は企画の経緯を、いきなり語り始めました。
transferCue: Describe starting a piece of music.
transferReply: The band launched into the final song.
transferReplyJapanese: バンドは最後の曲を、勢いよく始めました。
nuance: Inseparable. It suggests suddenness and length, so it is often mildly critical of a speech.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。突然さと長さを含意し、話について使うとやや批判的になる。
contrast: Launch into starts energetically; dive into stresses eagerness rather than length.
contrastJapanese: launch into は勢いよく始める。dive into は長さより熱意を強調する。

meaning: Criticise or attack someone strongly.
japanese: 激しく非難する。
cue: A review meeting became harsh. Describe it.
reply: The client laid into us about the delay.
replyJapanese: 顧客は遅延について、激しく非難してきました。
transferCue: Describe a critical newspaper column.
transferReply: The piece lays into the whole policy.
transferReplyJapanese: その記事は、政策全体を厳しく批判しています。
nuance: Inseparable and informal. Lay is irregular: laid. Strong, so keep it for real criticism.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できないくだけた表現。lay は不規則変化で laid。強い語なので、本当の非難に使う。
contrast: Lay into attacks verbally at length; tell off is a shorter reprimand.
contrastJapanese: lay into は長く激しく責める。tell off はもっと短い叱責。

meaning: Encourage someone to believe something that is not true.
japanese: 期待を持たせて、思わせぶりにする。
cue: A supplier implied a discount that never existed. Describe it.
reply: They led us on about the price for weeks.
replyJapanese: 先方は何週間も、価格について思わせぶりな態度を取りました。
transferCue: Warn against giving false hope.
transferReply: Don't lead him on if you've already decided.
transferReplyJapanese: もう決めているなら、彼に期待を持たせないでください。
nuance: Separable: lead them on. Lead is irregular: led. Always disapproving.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：lead them on。lead は不規則変化で led。つねに否定的。
contrast: Lead on creates false hope; put off discourages someone instead.
contrastJapanese: lead on は偽りの期待を与える。put off は逆に気をそぐこと。

meaning: Turn the pages of something quickly.
japanese: ページをぱらぱらとめくって見る。
cue: You looked at a book without reading it properly.
reply: I leafed through it in the shop and put it back.
replyJapanese: 店でぱらぱら見て、棚に戻しました。
transferCue: Describe waiting in a reception area.
transferReply: He leafed through a magazine for ten minutes.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は10分ほど、雑誌をめくっていました。
nuance: Inseparable. Only for things with pages, and it implies no real reading.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。ページのあるものにだけ使い、きちんと読んでいないことを含意する。
contrast: Leaf through skims pages; pore over studies them closely.
contrastJapanese: leaf through はぱらぱら見る。pore over はじっくり読み込む。

meaning: Accept an opportunity eagerly and at once.
japanese: 好機に、すぐ飛びつく。
cue: A colleague was offered a secondment. Describe the response.
reply: She leapt at the chance to work abroad.
replyJapanese: 海外で働く機会に、彼女はすぐ飛びつきました。
transferCue: Describe your own reaction to an offer.
transferReply: I'd leap at an offer like that.
transferReplyJapanese: そんな話なら、私ならすぐ飛びつきます。
nuance: Inseparable. Both leapt and leaped are used. Almost always with chance, opportunity or offer.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。過去形は leapt と leaped の両方がある。chance、opportunity、offer とともに使うことがほとんど。
contrast: Leap at accepts eagerly; jump on can mean seizing on someone's mistake.
contrastJapanese: leap at は喜んで受ける。jump on は人の失敗につけ込む意味にもなる。

meaning: Become less strong, or stop for a while.
japanese: 勢いが弱まる。一時的にやむ。
cue: Heavy rain has continued all day. Comment.
reply: If the rain lets up we could still go.
replyJapanese: 雨が弱まれば、まだ行けますよ。
transferCue: Describe a demanding period at work.
transferReply: The pressure hasn't let up since January.
transferReplyJapanese: 1月から、重圧が途切れていません。
nuance: Intransitive. Used for weather, pressure and effort, and often in the negative.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。天候や重圧、努力について使い、否定形になることも多い。
contrast: Let up is something easing on its own; ease up is a person doing less.
contrastJapanese: let up は自然に弱まること。ease up は人が手を緩めること。

meaning: Stop rising or falling and stay steady.
japanese: 変動が止まり、安定する。
cue: A rising cost has stabilised. Report it.
reply: Prices levelled off in the second half.
replyJapanese: 価格は後半、横ばいになりました。
transferCue: Describe a plane after take-off.
transferReply: The plane levelled off at thirty thousand feet.
transferReplyJapanese: 飛行機は3万フィートで水平飛行に移りました。
nuance: Intransitive. British doubles the l: levelled. Level out is an equally common variant.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。イギリス英語では levelled と l を重ねる。level out も同じくらい使う。
contrast: Level off stops changing; fall back means returning to a lower level.
contrastJapanese: level off は変動が止まる。fall back は低い水準に戻ること。

meaning: Stay in bed later than usual.
japanese: いつもより遅くまで寝ている。
cue: A friend asks about your Sunday.
reply: I lie in on Sundays and make a proper breakfast.
replyJapanese: 日曜は遅くまで寝て、しっかり朝食を作ります。
transferCue: Describe a rare morning off.
transferReply: We lay in until ten for the first time in months.
transferReplyJapanese: 何か月ぶりかに、10時まで寝ていました。
nuance: Intransitive and British; the noun is a lie-in. Lie is irregular: lay, lain.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞でイギリス英語。名詞は a lie-in。lie は不規則変化で lay、lain。
contrast: Lie in stays in bed by choice; sleep in can also mean oversleeping.
contrastJapanese: lie in は意図して長く寝ること。sleep in は寝過ごす意味にもなる。

meaning: Do gentle exercises to prepare your body.
japanese: 軽く体をほぐして、準備する。
cue: You are about to start a run with a friend.
reply: Let's limber up before we start.
replyJapanese: 始める前に、少し体をほぐしましょう。
transferCue: Describe a musician before a concert.
transferReply: She limbers up her hands before every performance.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は演奏のたびに、手をほぐします。
nuance: Intransitive. About loosening muscles specifically, not general preparation.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。一般的な準備ではなく、筋肉をほぐすことを指す。
contrast: Limber up loosens the body; warm up can also mean preparing an audience or a machine.
contrastJapanese: limber up は体をほぐす。warm up は観客や機械の準備にも使う。

meaning: Join with someone or something to work together.
japanese: 連携して、つながる。
cue: Two teams will collaborate next month. Describe it.
reply: We link up with the Osaka office in October.
replyJapanese: 10月に、大阪の事務所と連携します。
transferCue: Describe meeting someone during a journey.
transferReply: We'll link up with them at the station.
transferReplyJapanese: 駅で彼らと合流します。
nuance: Intransitive with with, or link something up. The noun is a link-up.
nuanceJapanese: with を伴う自動詞用法と、link something up の用法がある。名詞は link-up。
contrast: Link up joins forces; team up stresses working as one group.
contrastJapanese: link up はつながること。team up はひとつの組として動くことを強調する。

meaning: Listen to a conversation you are not part of.
japanese: 自分が当事者でない会話を、そばで聞く。
cue: You want to observe a call without speaking.
reply: Can I listen in on the handover call?
replyJapanese: 引き継ぎの通話に、聞き役として参加してもいいですか。
transferCue: Describe overhearing a discussion.
transferReply: I listened in for a minute and left.
transferReplyJapanese: 少しだけ聞いて、その場を離れました。
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces the conversation. Asking permission makes it polite rather than intrusive.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、会話は on で示す。許可を取れば、盗み聞きではなく同席の意味になる。
contrast: Listen in joins as an observer; eavesdrop is always secret.
contrastJapanese: listen in は聞き役として加わる。eavesdrop はつねに盗み聞き。

meaning: Make something more lively, or become more lively.
japanese: 活気づける。活気づく。
cue: A quiet gathering improved after music started.
reply: The evening livened up once the music started.
replyJapanese: 音楽が始まってから、夜は一気に活気づきました。
transferCue: Suggest improving a dull presentation.
transferReply: A short video would liven it up.
transferReplyJapanese: 短い動画があれば、もっと活気が出ます。
nuance: Separable: liven it up, or intransitive. About atmosphere and energy.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：liven it up。自動詞としても使う。雰囲気や活気についての語。
contrast: Liven up adds energy; jazz up adds visual or surface appeal.
contrastJapanese: liven up は活気を足す。jazz up は見た目の魅力を足す。

meaning: Put something in a locked place for safety.
japanese: 鍵をかけて、しまい込む。
cue: Valuables need storing during building work.
reply: We locked away the documents until the work finished.
replyJapanese: 工事が終わるまで、書類は鍵をかけて保管しました。
transferCue: Describe keeping medicine safe.
transferReply: Lock it away where the children can't reach.
transferReplyJapanese: 子どもの手が届かない場所に、鍵をかけて保管してください。
nuance: Separable: lock it away. Also used figuratively about keeping feelings hidden.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：lock it away。感情を内に閉じ込める比喩としても使う。
contrast: Lock away stores securely; lock out leaves someone unable to get in.
contrastJapanese: lock away は安全にしまう。lock out は中に入れなくすること。

meaning: Watch something without taking part.
japanese: 加わらずに、そばで見ている。
cue: Describe bystanders at an incident.
reply: A crowd looked on while the staff cleared the road.
replyJapanese: 係員が道を片づけるあいだ、人々はただ見ていました。
transferCue: Describe a coach during a match.
transferReply: He looked on from the side without shouting.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は声を出さず、脇から見守っていました。
nuance: Intransitive. It implies not intervening, which can sound passive.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。介入しないことを含意し、受け身な印象になることがある。
contrast: Look on watches without acting; look after takes responsibility for someone.
contrastJapanese: look on は何もせず見ている。look after は世話をする責任を負う。

meaning: Manage to succeed despite having no clear plan.
japanese: 手探りでも、なんとか切り抜ける。
cue: A task was done without proper instructions. Describe it.
reply: We had no manual, so we muddled through.
replyJapanese: 手引きがなかったので、手探りで何とかしました。
transferCue: Describe a first attempt at cooking something.
transferReply: I muddled through and it tasted fine.
transferReplyJapanese: 手探りで作りましたが、味は悪くありませんでした。
nuance: Intransitive and British. Modest rather than proud: it admits the process was messy.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞でイギリス英語。誇るより謙遜する言い方で、過程が雑だったことを認める。
contrast: Muddle through succeeds without a plan; make do manages with limited resources.
contrastJapanese: muddle through は計画なしに切り抜ける。make do は限られたもので間に合わせる。

meaning: Eat something in small bites, or show slight interest.
japanese: 少しずつかじる。わずかに関心を示す。
cue: Someone is not eating much at dinner. Describe it.
reply: She nibbled at the bread and left the rest.
replyJapanese: 彼女はパンを少しかじって、残しました。
transferCue: Describe a buyer's early interest.
transferReply: Two buyers are nibbling at the offer.
transferReplyJapanese: 2社が、その条件に少し関心を示しています。
nuance: Inseparable. Literal for food, figurative for tentative interest or slow reduction.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。食べ物には文字どおり、関心や減少には比喩的に使う。
contrast: Nibble at takes small bites; wolf down eats very quickly.
contrastJapanese: nibble at は少しずつかじる。wolf down は一気に食べる。

meaning: Achieve a number of wins or results.
japanese: 勝利や実績を、積み上げる。
cue: A team has reached a milestone. Report it.
reply: They notched up their hundredth sale this week.
replyJapanese: 今週、彼らは100件目の販売を達成しました。
transferCue: Describe a long-running show.
transferReply: The play has notched up five hundred performances.
transferReplyJapanese: その舞台は、500回の公演を重ねました。
nuance: Separable: notch them up. Used with countable achievements such as wins or sales.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：notch them up。勝利や販売など、数えられる実績と使う。
contrast: Notch up counts achievements; chalk up can also record a loss as experience.
contrastJapanese: notch up は実績を数える。chalk up は失敗を教訓として記録する意味にもなる。

meaning: Stop doing something, or attract a large number of people.
japanese: やめる。また、大勢を呼び込む。
cue: A friend is considering leaving a long-held job.
reply: He's thinking of packing in the commute and working locally.
replyJapanese: 彼は通勤をやめて、近くで働くことを考えています。
transferCue: Describe a popular venue.
transferReply: That little theatre packs in three hundred a night.
transferReplyJapanese: あの小さな劇場は、一晩に300人を集めます。
nuance: Separable: pack it in. British and informal. Pack it in! also means stop that.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：pack it in。くだけたイギリス英語。pack it in! は「やめて」という意味にもなる。
contrast: Pack in quits something; pack up can mean finishing for the day or breaking down.
contrastJapanese: pack in はやめること。pack up は片づける、あるいは故障する意味。

meaning: Reduce something to what is essential.
japanese: 必要な分だけに、削り込む。
cue: A document is too long for its audience.
reply: Let's pare it down to two pages.
replyJapanese: 2ページまで削りましょう。
transferCue: Describe simplifying a household.
transferReply: We pared down our things before the move.
transferReplyJapanese: 引っ越し前に、持ち物を減らしました。
nuance: Separable: pare it down. To introduces what remains. Slightly formal.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：pare it down。残す量は to で示す。やや改まった表現。
contrast: Pare down removes the inessential; cut back reduces an amount or an activity.
contrastJapanese: pare down は不要な部分を削ぐ。cut back は量や活動を減らす。

meaning: Blame someone for something, often unfairly.
japanese: 責任を、その人になすりつける。
cue: One person was blamed for a shared failure. Describe it.
reply: They pinned the whole delay on the newest member.
replyJapanese: 遅れの責任を、彼らは最も新しいメンバーに押しつけました。
transferCue: Refuse to accept misplaced blame.
transferReply: Don't pin that on me — I raised it in March.
transferReplyJapanese: 私のせいにしないでください。3月に指摘しています。
nuance: The thing blamed goes between pin and on. It usually implies the blame is unfair.
nuanceJapanese: 責任の内容は pin と on のあいだに置く。ふつうは不当な押しつけを含意する。
contrast: Pin on assigns blame to a person; put down to explains a cause without blame.
contrastJapanese: pin on は人に責任を負わせる。put down to は責めずに原因を説明する。

meaning: Suddenly speak, often after being silent.
japanese: 黙っていた人が、ふいに口を開く。
cue: A quiet person made the key point. Describe it.
reply: Then Ken piped up with the obvious answer.
replyJapanese: そのとき健さんが口を開いて、当たり前の答えを言いました。
transferCue: Describe a child joining an adult conversation.
transferReply: She piped up from the back seat.
transferReplyJapanese: 後部座席から、彼女がふいに声を上げました。
nuance: Intransitive; with introduces what was said. Informal and slightly affectionate.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、発言内容は with で示す。くだけた、やや親しみのある表現。
contrast: Pipe up breaks a silence; speak up means saying it louder or more assertively.
contrastJapanese: pipe up は沈黙を破る。speak up は大きく、はっきり言うこと。

meaning: Join in and help with a shared task.
japanese: みんなの作業に加わって、手伝う。
cue: A group is clearing up after an event.
reply: If everyone pitches in we'll be done by six.
replyJapanese: 全員が手伝えば、6時には終わります。
transferCue: Thank neighbours after a working day.
transferReply: Four neighbours pitched in and it took half the time.
transferReplyJapanese: 近所の4人が手伝ってくれて、半分の時間で済みました。
nuance: Intransitive; with introduces the task. Warm and informal, about shared effort.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、作業は with で示す。共同作業についての、温かくくだけた表現。
contrast: Pitch in joins a shared effort; help out can be helping one person.
contrastJapanese: pitch in は共同作業に加わる。help out は一人を手伝う場合にも使う。

meaning: Keep working steadily at something difficult.
japanese: 地道に、こつこつ続ける。
cue: Progress is slow but continuing. Describe it.
reply: We're plugging away at the backlog.
replyJapanese: たまった作業を、こつこつ片づけています。
transferCue: Describe learning an instrument.
transferReply: I plug away at it for twenty minutes a day.
transferReplyJapanese: 1日20分ずつ、地道に続けています。
nuance: Intransitive; at introduces the task. It accepts slow progress without complaint.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、対象は at で示す。進みの遅さを不満なく受け入れる響き。
contrast: Plug away continues steadily; press on stresses continuing despite obstacles.
contrastJapanese: plug away は地道に続ける。press on は障害があっても進むことを強調する。

meaning: Choose one option after hesitating.
japanese: 迷った末に、ひとつに決める。
cue: You could not decide between two dishes.
reply: In the end I plumped for the fish.
replyJapanese: 結局、魚のほうにしました。
transferCue: Describe choosing a colour.
transferReply: We plumped for the darker green.
transferReplyJapanese: 濃いほうの緑に決めました。
nuance: Inseparable, informal and British. It implies hesitation before the choice.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない、くだけたイギリス英語。決める前に迷ったことを含意する。
contrast: Plump for chooses after hesitating; settle on suggests the search is finally over.
contrastJapanese: plump for は迷った末に選ぶ。settle on は探し終えて落ち着く含み。

meaning: Improve something that is already reasonably good.
japanese: ある程度できているものを、さらに磨く。
cue: A draft is nearly ready but needs care.
reply: I'll polish up the wording before it goes out.
replyJapanese: 送る前に、言い回しを整えます。
transferCue: Describe preparing a language skill.
transferReply: She polished up her French before the trip.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は旅行前に、フランス語を磨き直しました。
nuance: Separable: polish it up. It assumes a working version already exists.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：polish it up。すでに形になっていることが前提。
contrast: Polish up refines what exists; flesh out adds missing substance.
contrastJapanese: polish up は既存のものを磨く。flesh out は足りない中身を足す。

meaning: Seize on something eagerly, especially a mistake.
japanese: すかさず飛びつく。あらを見つけて突く。
cue: A small error drew immediate criticism. Describe it.
reply: The press pounced on the one wrong figure.
replyJapanese: 報道は、間違った数字ひとつにすかさず飛びつきました。
transferCue: Describe a buyer reacting to a listing.
transferReply: Someone pounced on it within an hour.
transferReplyJapanese: 1時間以内に、誰かがすぐ手を出しました。
nuance: Inseparable. It suggests speed and eagerness, often to criticise.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。素早さと勢いを含意し、批判の文脈で使うことが多い。
contrast: Pounce on seizes eagerly; jump at is about accepting an opportunity.
contrastJapanese: pounce on は勢いよく飛びつく。jump at は機会を喜んで受けること。

meaning: Demand something repeatedly and firmly.
japanese: 繰り返し強く求める。
cue: A group wants a clear answer from management. Describe it.
reply: The union is pressing for a written commitment.
replyJapanese: 組合は、書面での約束を強く求めています。
transferCue: Describe asking for a refund.
transferReply: I pressed for a full refund and got one.
transferReplyJapanese: 全額返金を強く求めて、認められました。
nuance: Inseparable; for introduces the demand. Firmer than ask for, without being rude.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、要求内容は for で示す。ask for より強いが、無礼ではない。
contrast: Press for demands persistently; push for stresses driving something forward.
contrastJapanese: press for は粘り強く要求する。push for は前に進めることを強調する。

meaning: Support something that would otherwise fail or fall.
japanese: 倒れないように、下支えする。
cue: One product funds a struggling business. Describe it.
reply: Exports have propped up the company for years.
replyJapanese: 輸出が何年も会社を支えてきました。
transferCue: Describe a fence after a storm.
transferReply: We propped up the fence with two posts.
transferReplyJapanese: 支柱を2本当てて、塀を支えました。
nuance: Separable: prop it up. Often mildly critical when it means keeping something alive artificially.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：prop it up。人為的に延命させる意味では、やや批判的になる。
contrast: Prop up keeps something from failing; back up supports a claim with evidence.
contrastJapanese: prop up は倒れないよう支える。back up は根拠で主張を支える。

meaning: Work something out by thinking hard.
japanese: 頭をひねって、解き明かす。
cue: An unclear instruction eventually made sense.
reply: It took an hour to puzzle out what they meant.
replyJapanese: 意図を読み解くのに、1時間かかりました。
transferCue: Describe reading an old handwritten letter.
transferReply: We puzzled out most of the words together.
transferReplyJapanese: 二人で、ほとんどの単語を解読しました。
nuance: Separable: puzzle it out. It emphasises effort on something deliberately unclear.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：puzzle it out。分かりにくいものに労力をかけることを強調する。
contrast: Puzzle out decodes something obscure; figure out is the everyday equivalent.
contrastJapanese: puzzle out は分かりにくいものを解読する。figure out はより日常的な語。
